text: You're taking a selfie with Mittens at noon.
Click. The whole sky switches off at once.
Its last light takes one more second to run out.
The stars were there all along.
Half the planet looks up at once.
Jupiter keeps glowing. It won't notice for over an hour.
The air has no time to cool.
Then the light that was five seconds late arrives.
Your selfie: stars over Midtown, at noon.
And the Sun? It went dark eight minutes before you saw it.
